articles.title: Normal Maps Without Extra Geometry: A Practical Texture Workflow
articles.excerpt: A normal map adds surface detail by changing how lighting responds to a surface, without changing the mesh silhouette. It stores surface directions as color values, which a material uses when calculat…
articles.body: A normal map adds surface detail by changing how lighting responds to a surface, without changing the mesh silhouette. It stores surface directions as color values, which a material uses when calculating light. That makes normal maps useful for fine texture detail; larger shapes that change an object’s outline still belong in the geometry. A practical workflow Start with the right source. Use a texture or photo with detail at the scale you want to see on the model. If the source has strong shadows or highlights, inspect the result carefully: baked lighting can be mistaken for surface shape. Generate and inspect the map. A 2D preview helps you catch obvious artifacts.

articles.title: Why Your LLM Can't Count the R's in 'Strawberry'
articles.excerpt: Ask a state-of-the-art language model a question a six-year-old can answer — how many R's are in "strawberry"? — and there's a decent chance it says two. The answer is three. The model has read more t…
articles.body: Ask a state-of-the-art language model a question a six-year-old can answer — how many R's are in "strawberry"? — and there's a decent chance it says two . The answer is three. The model has read more text than any human who has ever lived. It can write working code, explain quantum mechanics, and pass the bar exam. But it trips over counting letters in a common word. This isn't a one-off glitch, and it isn't a sign the model is "dumb." It's a direct, predictable consequence of how language models read text in the first place. Once you understand tokenization , the strawberry problem stops being funny-mysterious and becomes obvious — and you'll understand a whole category of weird LLM behavior along with it. Models don't see letters. They see tokens.

articles.title: Advanced Webhook Operations & Resiliency: Architecture Patterns for Production Engineers
articles.excerpt: Webhooks are the main way SaaS platforms, payment processors and internal microservices tell other systems that something happened. At a few thousand events a day, a loop that POSTs to a URL and retri…
articles.body: Webhooks are the main way SaaS platforms, payment processors and internal microservices tell other systems that something happened. At a few thousand events a day, a loop that POSTs to a URL and retries on failure is enough. At hundreds of millions of events a day, the same loop turns small outages into large ones. Retries pile up, healthy customers get starved by unhealthy ones, and the infrastructure sitting in front of your consumers starts rejecting requests for reasons your application never sees. This guide covers four areas of production webhook operations: Adaptive backoff combined with per-endpoint circuit breakers . Preventing retry storms and cascading failures. Zero-downtime migration of delivery infrastructure and payload schemas.

articles.body: Convert TTF/OTF fonts to WOFF2 in the browser (no install, no upload server) You designed a landing page. The brand font is a .ttf sitting on your desktop. Chrome DevTools is already complaining about font payload. You need WOFF2 — and you do not want to install FontTools, pay for a desktop app, or upload the file to a random converter that keeps a copy. This post is a short, practical path: what WOFF2 is, when to use it, and how to convert TTF/OTF → WOFF2 entirely in the browser . Why WOFF2 still matters Smaller than TTF/OTF for the same glyphs (Brotli-based compression). Widely supported in evergreen browsers for @font-face . Better for Core Web Vitals when you also subset and use font-display .

Credit: NASA The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions. articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.
